item.title: Trump's Situation Room meeting on Iran ends without deal
item.description:
President Donald Trump convened a high-stakes meeting in the White House Situation Room on Friday to make what he called a "final determination" on a proposed memorandum of understanding with Iran, but the nearly two-hour session ended without a resolution, according to The New York Times.

The meeting came after Trump announced his plans in a Truth Social post Friday morning, writing, "I will be meeting now, in the Situation Room, to make a final determination". He outlined preconditions for any agreement, insisting that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb" and that the Strait of Hormuz must "immediately open" to unrestricted shipping with no tolls.

item.title: Rubio thanks Pakistan for Iran mediation efforts
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the State Department on Friday, with discussions centering on Pakistan's role mediating the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and the broader bilateral relationship between Washington and Islamabad.

item.title: Ebola funding pledges nearly halved as outbreak spreads
item.description:
International financial commitments to combat the Ebola outbreak in Central and East Africa have nearly halved in a matter of days, Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya revealed Thursday, as the deadly Bundibugyo strain continues to spread through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda with no approved vaccine available.

Speaking from Kinshasa, Kaseya said pledges that stood at nearly $500 million on Monday, May 25, had dropped to approximately $290 million by Thursday after multiple donors withdrew their commitments. The collapse in funding represents a loss of roughly $210 million at a moment when the outbreak has grown to more than 1,000 suspected cases and 246 deaths in the DRC alone.

item.title: Quarter of trapped oil tankers slip out of Hormuz
item.description: A slow, stealthy trickle of oil tankers has begun slipping out of the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, with roughly one-quarter of the large non-Iranian vessels stranded since the war began now having crossed the chokepoint, even as Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned that ships continue to come under attack.

item.title: Philippines says China threat persists despite Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The Philippines' defense secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said on Saturday that the country remains under "severe threat" from China, declaring that a recent thaw in U.S.-China relations following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing has done nothing to ease tensions in the South China Sea.

item.title: Lula rejects U.S. terrorist label for Brazil's largest gangs
item.description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Friday denounced the United States' decision to designate two of Brazil's largest criminal organizations as terrorist groups, calling it undue interference in the country's internal affairs and warning Washington against treating Brazil "like a banana republic."

"We will not accept being treated like children, we will not accept being treated as if we were a banana republic," Lula said at a public event on Friday, referring to "a certain Marco Rubio, who said that our criminals are terrorists and that Americans can intervene".

item.title: Blast at explosives storage site kills dozens in Myanmar
item.description: An explosion at a building storing mining explosives in northeastern Myanmar killed at least 46 people on Sunday, including six children, with local media reporting death tolls as high as 55. About 70 others were injured in the blast, which struck around noon in the village of Kaungtup in Namhkam township, roughly two miles from the Chinese border.

item.title: Trump returned Iran peace draft with stricter conditions
item.description: President Donald Trump returned a revised draft of a proposed peace agreement to Tehran with stricter conditions after a two-hour meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on Friday, extending negotiations into at least another week, according to multiple reports.

item.title: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle in deepest Lebanon incursion in 25 years
item.description: Israeli forces have captured the medieval Beaufort Castle and pushed past the Litani River into southern Lebanon, marking the country's deepest ground incursion into its northern neighbor in more than 25 years. The advance, confirmed by the Israeli military on Sunday, has shattered a fragile ceasefire and drawn sweeping evacuation orders covering much of southern Lebanon.

item.title: Hegseth warns U.S. ready to resume strikes on Iran if talks fail
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned Saturday that the United States is fully prepared to restart military operations against Iran if ongoing ceasefire negotiations collapse, delivering a pointed message at the Shangri-La Dialogue security forum in Singapore as tensions in the region escalated with a fresh Iranian missile strike on a base housing American personnel.

item.title: Taiwan vows not to be 'silenced' after China expels NYT reporter
item.description: Taiwan's Presidential Office on Sunday condemned China's expulsion of New York Times correspondent Vivian Wang, declaring the island democracy "will not be silenced because of oppression" and vowing to continue engaging with international media despite Beijing's pressure campaign against foreign journalists.

item.title: Iran's Pezeshkian reportedly resigns, citing IRGC takeover
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reportedly submitted a formal letter of resignation to the office of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, claiming he has been systematically excluded from key decision-making and that hardline factions within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps have seized control of government affairs, according to Iran International, which cited an anonymous Iranian official. Iranian authorities quickly denied the report.

item.title: France detains 780 after deadly riots follow PSG's Champions League win
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain's second consecutive Champions League title — sealed in a dramatic penalty shootout against Arsenal in Budapest on Saturday — triggered one of the most violent nights of football-related disorder France has seen, with 780 people arrested and one person found dead on the Paris ring road.

item.title: France seizes sanctioned Russian tanker in Atlantic
item.description: The French Navy boarded and detained the sanctioned oil tanker Tagor on Sunday, May 31, in international waters of the Atlantic Ocean, in the latest Western crackdown on Russia's so-called shadow fleet used to evade energy export restrictions.

item.title: US and Iran exchange strikes as Trump pushes tougher deal terms
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared early Monday that Iran "really wants to make a deal" with the United States, posting on Truth Social even as both countries exchanged fresh military strikes near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend — the latest escalation in a three-month-old conflict that continues to complicate diplomatic efforts.

U.S. Central Command said it struck Iranian military sites along the coast in response to "provocative Iranian actions, including the downing of a U.S. MQ-1 drone operating in international waters." Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded on Monday by claiming a retaliatory strike on a U.S. base, according to Reuters.

item.title: CERN finds high-significance hint of physics beyond the Standard Model
item.description: Physicists working at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have found what may be one of the strongest hints yet that the Standard Model of particle physics is incomplete, publishing results that show rare "penguin" decays of subatomic particles behaving in ways current theory cannot explain. The discovery arrives as the LHC prepares to shut down for its High-Luminosity upgrade — a project now clouded by the United Kingdom's decision to pull funding.

item.title: Kuwait intercepts Iranian missiles as US-Iran strikes escalate near Hormuz
item.description: The United States and Iran exchanged fresh military strikes over the weekend, with Kuwait caught in the crossfire early Monday after Iranian missiles and drones targeted a US air base on its territory, marking another volatile chapter in the three-month-old conflict even as both sides signal a desire to negotiate.

item.title: Nvidia unveils RTX Spark, its first Windows PC chip in over a decade
item.description: Nvidia officially unveiled the RTX Spark at its GTC Taipei keynote on Sunday evening, marking the company's first consumer Windows PC processor in over a decade and a direct challenge to Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm in the laptop market.

item.title: Iran halts US talks over Israel's escalation in Lebanon
item.description: Iran announced on Monday that it would suspend indirect negotiations and message exchanges with the United States through mediators, citing Israel's intensified military operations in Lebanon as a violation of ceasefire conditions. The move threatens to upend weeks of fragile diplomacy aimed at ending the broader conflict between Washington and Tehran.

item.title: Armenia's Pashinyan rejects Russia's call for EU referendum
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin called Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Sunday to congratulate him on his 51st birthday, a gesture of diplomatic courtesy that contrasted sharply with the escalating pressure Moscow has placed on Yerevan in recent weeks over its pursuit of closer ties with the European Union.
